h: Heinz bodies and hemolysis after an oxidant drug: deficient enzyme?
p: G6PD (X-linked) supplies NADPH via the pentose phosphate pathway to protect RBCs from oxidants; smear shows Heinz bodies and bite cells.

x: keyed mechanism (type III) disputable vs type IV granulomas

h: Beta-thalassemia major: cause of hepatosplenomegaly?
p: Ineffective erythropoiesis drives marrow expansion (crew-cut skull) and extramedullary hematopoiesis in liver and spleen; iron overload follows transfusions.

h: Lacunar stroke of the subthalamic nucleus: finding?
p: Subthalamic lesions release inhibition of the thalamus, causing violent flinging movements on the opposite side. Parkinsonian rigidity comes from substantia nigra loss.

h: Exercise, fish diet, moderate wine: which lipoprotein rises?
p: Exercise, moderate alcohol and unsaturated fats raise HDL; smoking, obesity and a sedentary lifestyle lower it.

h: Psychosis lasting under one month after severe stress, then full recovery: diagnosis?
p: Brief psychotic disorder: 1 day to 1 month, often after a stressor; schizophreniform is 1-6 months; schizophrenia needs 6 months.

h: Hypertension with low potassium and high-normal sodium: best drug?
p: Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome): hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, low renin; aldosterone antagonists treat bilateral disease, surgery for adenoma.

h: Neprilysin inhibition raises which peptides?
p: Neprilysin degrades natriuretic peptides and bradykinin; sacubitril (with valsartan) treats heart failure. Do not combine with ACE inhibitors (angioedema).

h: L5-S1 disc herniation (S1 root): exam finding?
d: Decreased sensation of the anterior thigh
p: S1 compression gives plantarflexion weakness, reduced ankle jerk and lateral foot sensory loss; L4 affects the patellar reflex and L5 causes foot drop.

h: Goodpasture syndrome: antibody target?
p: Anti-GBM antibodies attack the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen in glomeruli and alveoli, giving rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and hemoptysis with linear IF.

h: Delayed cord separation, recurrent infections with no pus: defect?
p: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1: absent CD18 integrin prevents tight adhesion and transmigration, so neutrophils are high in blood and absent at infection sites.

h: Perianal itching, tape test shows ova: treatment?
p: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm): treat with mebendazole, albendazole or pyrantel pamoate, and treat household contacts.

h: Calcified liver cyst with daughter cysts, animal contact: organism?
p: Hydatid cyst from dog tapeworm: spillage can cause anaphylaxis; treat with albendazole and careful surgery.

h: Acute angle-closure glaucoma: drug to avoid?
p: Mydriatics and anticholinergics worsen angle closure; treat with acetazolamide, topical beta-blockers, pilocarpine and definitive laser iridotomy.

h: Hyperprolactinemia with amenorrhea: drug of choice?
p: Dopamine agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine) suppress prolactin and shrink prolactinomas; metoclopramide is a D2 antagonist that raises prolactin.

h: Bronchiectasis, sinusitis, dextrocardia: associated finding?
p: Kartagener (primary ciliary dyskinesia, dynein arm defect): infertility or ectopic pregnancy risk from immotile cilia and sperm.

h: RNA splicing removes what?
p: Spliceosomes (snRNPs) excise introns and join exons; splice-site mutations in beta-globin cause beta-thalassemia.

h: Lace-like rash with circumoral pallor in a child: virus infects which cells?
p: Parvovirus B19 (erythema infectiosum, fifth disease) infects erythroid precursors via P antigen, causing aplastic crisis in hemolytic anemias and hydrops fetalis.

h: Low PAPP-A, high beta-hCG at age 38: diagnostic confirmation?
a: Extra chromosome in placental tissue (CVS karyotype)
p: First-trimester screening suggests trisomy 21; chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis karyotype is diagnostic. Quad screen markers are screening only.

h: SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction: which antidepressant to switch to?
p: Bupropion (NDRI) has minimal sexual side effects; avoid in seizure disorders and eating disorders. Other SSRIs share the problem.

h: Huntington disease: which neurotransmitter is relatively increased?
p: Striatal loss lowers GABA and ACh, leaving dopamine relatively increased (chorea); tetrabenazine depletes dopamine. N-acetyl aspartate falls with neuronal loss.

h: SLE with pleuritic chest pain and friction rub: diagnosis?
p: Serositis is common in lupus (pericarditis, pleuritis); pericarditis causes positional pain relieved by leaning forward, diffuse ST elevation and PR depression.

h: Obturator nerve injury: which muscle is weakened?
p: The obturator nerve supplies the medial thigh adductors; tensor fasciae latae is superior gluteal nerve and semitendinosus is tibial (sciatic).

h: Thin athlete, BMI 16, amenorrhea: bone complication?
p: Female athlete triad: low energy availability, amenorrhea (low estrogen) and osteoporosis; increases stress fracture risk.

x: acute drug choice disputable (propranolol vs thionamide)

h: Unvaccinated child stays healthy because community is immune: phenomenon?
p: When enough people are vaccinated, transmission falls and protects the unvaccinated; thresholds depend on R0 (about 95 percent for measles).
